issueTitle: Queries with nested lambdas (FILTER/MAP/array filter) return the first execution's results when re-run with different captured values
reporterNeed: Run the same LINQ query shape twice with a different captured variable inside a nested lambda over an array (e.g. `col.Query().Where(n => n.ListB.Where(t => t.Key == "x" && t.Values[0] == v).Any())` with `v = "a"` then `"b"`) and get results for the current value. Instead every later run silently returned the first run's results, for the whole process lifetime — across new `LiteDatabase` instances, file reopen and `Rebuild()`. Silent wrong data, present since 5.0.5, reported on 5.0.9/5.0.15/5.0.17+ on .NET Framework 4.8 and .NET.
suggestedAction: Add a LINQ-level regression test that replicates the reporters' own code — `col.Query().Where(n => n.ListB.Where(t => t.Key == "x" && t.Values[0] == v).Any())` with `v = "a"` then `"b"` and in reverse order, plus the `Children.Where(c => c.Name.Contains(x)).Any()` (#1897) and `contacts.Select(c => ids.Contains(c.id)).Any(t => t)` (#2408) shapes — since all three reporters hit this through LINQ and nothing currently pins that path. When the PR lands, post on #2800 (and the three duplicates) the root cause, the fixed version, and that no data was corrupted — only query results were wrong.
whatChanged: The internal `BsonExpression.Execute`/`ExecuteScalar` gained an optional `BsonDocument parameters` argument used as `parameters ?? this.Parameters`, and every site that runs an embedded inner expression now forwards the runtime parameters it already receives: `MAP`, `FILTER`, `SORT` (BsonExpressionFunctions.cs:18/32/47) and `ARRAY_INDEX`, `ARRAY_FILTER` (BsonExpressionOperators.cs:288/328). I checked those five are the complete set — they are the only runtime functions taking a `BsonExpression`, and the parser's only inner-expression embeddings (`Expression.Constant` at BsonExpressionParser.cs:720, 1053, 1144) feed exactly them. For the reporter's query: LINQ re-parses per call with a fresh parameters document (LinqExpressionVisitor.cs:75), the outer cached delegate receives it as its lambda argument, and it now reaches the stale cached inner lambda instead of the inner's own parse-time document. `v = "b"` now returns id 2. The inner's `Parameters` is not mutated, so the shared cached instance stays thread-safe.

gap: Narrow leftovers, all pre-existing rather than new: `GenerateIndexName` still has no fallback when the filtered source is empty (a field whose name is all punctuation or an astral-plane emoji, e.g. `$["🔥"]`, still yields "" and the same `ArgumentNullException: Value cannot be null. (Parameter 'name')` #2138 originally reported), no leading-digit guard (`$["2fa"]` -> "2fa" -> `InvalidIndexName ... Use only [a-Z$_]`), and no truncation to INDEX_NAME_MAX_LENGTH (32), so a long property name still throws `MaxLength = 32`. issueTitle: EnsureIndex(x => x.Prop) generates an empty or colliding index name for non-ASCII field names and under the Turkish (tr-TR) culture

Cost every user pays: each auto-named `EnsureIndex` now materialises the whole `$indexes` catalog first — `SysIndexes` opens a read snapshot per collection in the database and `.ToDocuments()` pulls every row before the in-memory `Where` on collection name. issueTitle: Parameterize Query helpers to avoid recompiling distinct literal values
reporterNeed: The real reporters (zangxq #2395 on 5.0.16, kimdiego2098 #2421 on 5.0.17, consolidated by the maintainer into #2807) ran long-lived loops/timers calling `col.DeleteMany(Query.EQ("Name", name))` / `DeleteMany(Query.LT("Date", cutoff))` with a new value each time and watched process memory grow forever, because each distinct value produced new expression text that was compiled into a never-evicted static cache. The existing `Query.EQ/LT/...` helpers are deliberately left embedding literals (a test pins that, to preserve their implicit-string / `ToSQL` contract). `Query.Compose` (Query.And/Or) now also deep-copies operand parameter values.

Their fatal symptom — unbounded growth — was already removed by #2772/90788ba, a different commit; this one adds nothing for them unless they rewrite their code to an API they have no way to discover: the literal helpers carry no XML-doc pointer to `Query.Parameterized`, and the compat rationale for not fixing them in place lives only in docs/memory-management-proposal.md, not in the issue or the public docs. overshoot: `Query.Compose` now runs `SnapshotQueryValue` on every operand parameter, so every `Query.And`/`Query.Or` — including compositions of LINQ-generated predicates that have nothing to do with this issue — deep-copies all parameter values (arrays, documents, byte[] binaries, float[] vectors are cloned) and freezes them at composition time. That is a new cost and a semantic change paid by all users, not requested by the report; test `Composition_snapshots_mutable_operand_parameter_values` pins the new semantics. Otherwise the change is additive (new public `Query.Parameterized` type, new public `QueryAny()` ctor) and does not alter existing behaviour.

issueTitle: After a disk-full IOException the LiteDatabase instance stays unusable, and some failure paths leak file handles
reporterNeed: Users (consolidated from #2286, #2108, #2614, #2615) hit `IOException: There is not enough space on the disk` during a write or auto-checkpoint on 5.0.10/5.0.15/5.0.21. They want to keep using the database after the disk recovers, and at minimum to be told what to do.
whatChanged: `EngineState.Handle` now stores, for `IOException` only, a new `IOException("Engine closed after an I/O failure. Dispose and reopen the database before retrying. " + ex.Message, ex)` instead of the raw exception, so every subsequent `Validate()` rethrow names the real condition and keeps the original as InnerException. `LiteEngine.Query` gained an eager `_state.Validate()` so read paths (`Count()`, `FindAll()`) surface that stored exception instead of `ObjectDisposedException(TransactionMonitor)` from the disposed monitor. The first throw at the point of failure is unchanged. Three tests assert the new message, that dispose/reopen recovers committed rows without deleting the WAL, and that a failed constructor releases the file (that last one is #2772 behaviour, re-asserted).
gap: The instance is still permanently dead: after space is freed the user must dispose and recreate `LiteDatabase`, which for the common DI-singleton usage is still their work — the commit explains the recovery rather than enabling it, exactly the part the maintainer's own comment said would stay open. The #2108 half of the consolidated report is untouched and untested: the auto-checkpoint runs after the transaction is already durable, so `Insert` still fails with a raw `IOException` for a document that was in fact committed, and a retry can still duplicate it — the new wrapper never appears on that first throw, so the caller has no way to distinguish "not written" from "written, checkpoint failed". The 5.0.21 `Rebuild()` path (orphan `<name>-temp.db`/`-log` left behind on a mid-rebuild disk-full, noted in the fork comment) is also not covered. Items 1-3 of the issue's own proposed fix landed in #2772; item 5 is still open, yet PR #2917 carries "Closes #2821".
overshoot: Small but real: for an IOException-closed engine the second-and-later throw is now a different exception object with a different HResult (COR_E_IO 0x80131620 rather than ERROR_HANDLE_DISK_FULL 0x70), so user code that matched on `HResult`, on exception identity, or on the exact message for those later calls stops matching; the `INVALID_DATAFILE_STATE` path is deliberately left unwrapped, so the two close reasons now behave inconsistently. The eager `Validate()` in `Query` also changes the post-`Dispose()` read failure from `ObjectDisposedException` to `LiteException(ENGINE_DISPOSED)` — consistent with every other engine entry point, but an observable type change on a path that was not broken. suggestedAction: Drop "Closes #2821" from PR #2917 (or immediately reopen/file a follow-up) and tell the reporters plainly what is and is not fixed: the message now says to dispose and reopen, the WAL must not be deleted, but the engine still cannot resume in place. Track the two remaining items separately — (a) a checkpoint failure after a successful commit must not be reported as the write failing (#2108 duplicate-insert hazard), and (b) `RebuildService` should delete the `-temp` data and log files when rebuild fails midway.

issueTitle: Rebuild() throws "Detected loop in FindAll({0})" when a collection with a secondary index has more than 2,550 documents
overshoot: Mild and contained, not enough to change the verdict. The guard is loosened on every write path, not only rebuild: all 8 `Detected loop` sites in IndexService/DataService now use `_maxItemsCount + NewPages.Count * 255`. `NewPages` also records pages taken from the free list (SnapShot.cs:413 adds every allocation, including `TryAllocateFreePage` hits), which are already counted in the file-length bound — so those are double-counted and the bound is looser than strictly needed. It is also transaction-wide, not per snapshot, so allocations for collection A raise the bound for collection B in the same transaction. Consequence: a genuine index/data cycle hit inside a large bulk write transaction now spins much longer before `ENSURE` fires. Bounded, never infinite. The second test pins that a real cycle still throws, including with a corrupted `LastPageID`. No new public API (`AdditionalTraversalItemsCount` is internal; `GetMonitor()` already existed), no changed defaults, no new exceptions, negligible per-traversal cost (one O(1) `List.Count` read, `uint`→`ulong` counter).
reporterNeed: Users on 5.0.19+ could no longer run `Rebuild()` (and auto-rebuild recovery) on healthy databases: any collection with a secondary index and more than 2,550 documents threw `LiteException: Detected loop in FindAll({0})`, and the exception closed the engine. whatChanged: Adds `Snapshot.AdditionalTraversalItemsCount = _transPages.NewPages.Count * 255` and adds it to the loop bound at every traversal guard in IndexService (AddNode, GetNodeList, DeleteAll, DeleteList, FindAll, Find) and DataService.Read. `NewPages` accumulates for the whole transaction and is not cleared by `Safepoint()` (TransactionService.Safepoint only resets `TransactionSize` and clears snapshot local pages), so during `RebuildContent`'s single transaction the bound grows with every page allocated for the inserted documents. `EnsureIndex` inside `RebuildContent` joins that same thread-bound transaction and therefore sees a bound of roughly `2550 + allocatedPages * 255`, which always exceeds the node count it walks. The reporter's 3,000-doc `FindAll` walk no longer trips the guard.

issueTitle: ObjectId uses fallback machine and process ids on net8.0/net10.0: HAVE_* symbols are never defined since #2771

issueTitle: Is there a way to get auto increment as "int?" insted of "int"?
reporterNeed: MoQuEs generates his model from Swagger/NSwag/AutoRest, which emits the Id property as `int?` rather than `int`, and he cannot get LiteDB's auto-increment to work with it. whatChanged: `RemoveDocId` (LiteDB/Client/Database/Collections/Insert.cs) now treats a BSON-null `_id` as "empty" for the Int32, Int64 and Guid auto-id modes, not only for ObjectId. Since `_id` is always serialized even when null (BsonMapper.SerializationErrors.cs:17 exempts `_id` from SerializeNullValues), an `int? Id = null` previously reached the engine as `_id: null` and was rejected by `LiteException.InvalidDataType("_id", null)` in Engine/Insert.cs; now the key is stripped, the engine's sequence generator assigns the next int, and the generated value is copied back into the entity via `_id.Setter` (the compiled setter unboxes the raw `int` into `int?` fine). `_autoId` was already resolved to `BsonAutoId.Int32` for `Int32?` in the LiteCollection ctor, and `AutoId` defaults to true, so no attribute is needed. The copy-back also moved into the shared `GetBsonDocs` iterator so single Insert, Insert(IEnumerable), Upsert and InsertBulk all behave the same.
gap: Nothing material for this report. LiteDB.Tests/Issues/Issue1002_Tests.cs uses exactly `public int? Id { get; set; }` with both `null` and `0`, asserts unique generated int keys, write-back into the entity, and persistence across reopen; AutoIdAssignment_Tests repeats it for `int?`/`long?`/`Guid?` across all five write paths (Insert, Insert(IEnumerable), Upsert x2, InsertBulk). overshoot: Two changes the report does not require, both low-risk: (1) a new pre-insert `LiteException.DataTypeNotAssignable` when auto-id is ObjectId, the setter is the default reflected one, and the Id member type cannot take an ObjectId (e.g. `string Id = null`). That path previously inserted the document and then threw InvalidCastException from the compiled setter, so it goes from "row persisted + opaque cast error" to "nothing persisted + typed error" — no previously-working path starts throwing, but the persisted-row side effect disappears. (2) For the single-entity `Insert(T)` path the Id write-back now runs inside the engine's enumeration, i.e. before commit, instead of after it; a throwing Id setter now rolls back the whole insert, and the entity's Id can be mutated before a commit that later fails. Both are pinned by tests (Custom_setter_can_copy_back_ObjectId_to_a_string_member, Throwing_setter_rolls_back_before_caller_can_commit) that issue 1002 does not justify — they belong to the other issues bundled into this commit. suggestedAction: Comment on the issue: as of this change `int?`/`long?`/`Guid?` Id members auto-generate for both null and default(T), and the generated value is written back into the entity, so Swagger/NSwag-generated models work unmodified — no attribute or mapper tweak needed. Nothing else to do for this issue.

issueTitle: duplicated key randomly pop
overshoot: Material, and mostly in the mechanism rather than the outcome. (a) Locking is implemented by passing side-effecting generators to `_files.Update(...)`: `WriteWithFileLock` yields no documents and does the real delete inside the generator, and `OpenWrite` calls `_files.Update(Enumerable.Empty<...>())` purely to take a lock. Correctness now depends on `LiteEngine.Update` enumerating lazily, inside the lock, exactly once. (b) To protect that, the commit adds a new documented contract to the public `ILiteEngine` interface ("must be consumed at most once... decorators must forward these sequences without pre-enumerating them"). Any existing third-party engine decorator that materialises `docs` (for logging, validation, batching) now silently loses the atomicity this commit promises, or runs the delete twice; a test pins this. (c) Every `OpenWrite` now pays an extra engine call plus a `_files` write-lock acquisition, on every upload. (d) New `ArgumentNullException` when a custom `TFileId` serialises to `BsonValue.Null` — a path that previously did something. (e) Engine-wide visibility change beyond storage: a cursor opened before a write upgrade in the same transaction no longer sees that transaction's own writes (`Issue1344SnapshotCursor_Tests` pins "old" after `UpdateMany`), while `Include` re-resolution in the same transaction does see them (`Issue1344IncludeRevisit_Tests` pins "new"). That split semantic, and the retained snapshots kept alive until transaction cleanup, are decisions the report never asked for. (f) 12 test files / ~1100 test lines for one 2019 report.
reporterNeed: On LiteDB 4.1.4 (Xamarin, UWP + Android) they download tweet images and store each one with `db.FileStorage.Upload("$/tweet/<name>.jpg", filename, stream)`, opening a fresh `LiteDatabase` per save. Roughly one call in four throws `Cannot insert duplicate key in unique index '_id'. The duplicate value is '{f:"$/tweet/EGyVJ_MU4AEM1k-.jpg", n:0}'`, followed by an unhandled NullReferenceException their try/catch cannot catch; their Debug output interleaves, so two saves are overlapping even though they believe the code is single-threaded. suggestedAction: Comment on #1344 with the honest answer, since it has had zero replies since 2019: the duplicate chunk key came from chunks left behind by an interrupted upload that the old `if (_file.Length > 0)` guard in the `LiteFileStream` write path refused to purge, plus two overlapping uploads to the same id racing between the `_files` and `_chunks` writes; both are addressed on v6 (821f5c25e + c5f489bbb3). Add the part the fix does not cover: in v5/v6 they must not open a new `LiteDatabase` per save from concurrent code — use one shared instance, or `Connection=Shared` — and their v4 NullReferenceException is not reproduced by anything here, so if it recurs on v6 it needs a fresh issue with a v6 stack trace.
whatChanged: This commit makes `LiteStorage.Delete` atomic (file record + chunks in one write transaction), forces `OpenWrite`/`SetMetadata`/`Delete` to take the `_files` write lock before touching `_chunks` so concurrent upload/delete/metadata cannot invert lock order, adds null-id validation, and in the engine retains a read snapshot (`Snapshot.RetainForCursor`) when a transaction upgrades a collection to write mode, so an already-open cursor keeps its original WAL view instead of running against a disposed snapshot. Worth noting: the actual root cause of the reporter's duplicate chunk key — the `if (_file.Length > 0)` guard that skipped purging orphan chunks, and the non-transactional Upload — was fixed in the PREVIOUS commit 821f5c25e (#2806). c5f489bbb3 adds the concurrency/atomicity hardening on top, which is what covers the overlapping-calls part of their trace.

issueTitle: [BUG] InvalidCastException From LiteDB.ObjectId To System.String
overshoot:
Three changes go past what #2590 needs (they serve the other issues bundled in the same commit, #1002/#2811):
1. `id.IsNull ||` was added to the Int32, Int64 and Guid branches of `RemoveDocId` (LiteDB/Client/Database/Collections/Insert.cs:95-98). Previously `int?`/`long?`/`Guid?` ids left as null reached the engine and threw `LiteException.InvalidDataType("_id", Null)` (LiteDB/Engine/Engine/Insert.cs:67); now they silently auto-generate. Behaviour flip on a path that used to throw — fine as a fix, but not asked for here, and pinned by `AutoIdAssignment_Tests.Nullable_ids_generate_for_null_and_empty_and_survive_reopen`.
2. The id copy-back setter now runs *inside* the engine's lazy enumeration, mid-transaction (the new `GetBsonDocs(T, BsonDocument)` iterator). A user-supplied Id setter that throws now aborts the ambient transaction: `AutoIdAssignment_Tests.Throwing_setter_rolls_back_before_caller_can_commit` pins that `db.Commit()` returns false after an explicit `BeginTrans()`, so unrelated work already queued in that user transaction is discarded too. Previously the row committed and only the setter blew up. Defensible, but it is a semantic change for every `Insert`/`Upsert`/`InsertBulk` caller, not just this reporter.
3. `MemberMapper.DefaultSetter` added (internal, so not public API surface) purely to let the new check distinguish a user-supplied setter.
The Issue2590 test itself hedges: it accepts *either* a working string auto-id *or* the rejection, and only the rejection branch actually executes — so it does not pin that the reporter gets what they asked for.
reporterNeed: On v5.0.21 they have a POCO with a `string Id` property whose parameterless-ish constructor sets `Id = string.Empty`, and they call `col.Insert(new RoflType("MyName"))` on `db.GetCollection<RoflType>()`. They expect the insert to work (presumably with LiteDB filling the id, Mongo-style); instead it throws `InvalidCastException` from `LiteDB.ObjectId` to `System.String`. No comments from anyone else; single scenario.
suggestedAction: Comment on #2590 with the honest answer the reporter never got, then close (or keep open only for the message wording): "LiteDB auto-generates `_id` only for ObjectId, Guid, Int32 and Int64. Your `Id` is a `string`, and because `BsonMapper.EmptyStringToNull` is on by default your `string.Empty` is stored as BSON null, which makes LiteDB think it must generate an id — it generates an ObjectId and cannot assign it back to a string. Fixes: assign the id yourself (`Id = ObjectId.NewObjectId().ToString()` or a Guid string), change `Id` to `ObjectId`/`Guid`/`int`, or register a custom `mapper.ResolveMember` setter for `Id` (see AutoIdAssignment_Tests.Custom_setter_can_copy_back_ObjectId_to_a_string_member)." Separately, make the new throw in Insert.cs:110 self-explanatory the way the read-only-member throw two lines above it already is — name the member and the cause, e.g. "Cannot generate an auto ID for member 'Id': generated ObjectId values cannot be assigned to System.String. Assign the id yourself or map it with a custom setter." Keeping the plain "Data type X is not assignable from data type Y" text is the one thing that leaves this reporter guessing.
whatChanged: `RemoveDocId` now pre-checks, before anything is written, that a generated ObjectId can actually be assigned to the id member: when `_autoId == BsonAutoId.ObjectId`, the setter is the mapper's own reflected setter, and `_id.DataType` is not assignable from `ObjectId`, it throws `LiteException.DataTypeNotAssignable` (code DATA_TYPE_NOT_ASSIGNABLE). For the reporter's `string Id` this replaces the old failure mode. Old behaviour: `_engine.Insert` committed the row with a generated ObjectId `_id`, and only then `_id.Setter(entity, id.RawValue)` threw `InvalidCastException` — leaving an orphan row in the collection that the typed collection could never find by its string key. New behaviour: nothing is written at all and a LiteDB-typed exception is raised. The insert still does not succeed.

issueTitle: [BUG] AesStream.Seek adds the hidden-page offset for Current and End origins
overshoot: Small, contained. Seek now throws three exceptions it never threw before: ArgumentException for an unknown SeekOrigin (previously delegated to the backing stream, which throws the same), IOException for any seek resolving to a negative logical position (previously silently landed inside the hidden 8192-byte header page — no internal LiteDB caller does this; AesStream is public, so a third party relying on that accident would now break, but the old behaviour was corrupting), and OverflowException from the two `checked` arithmetic sites. OverflowException is not part of the documented Stream.Seek contract (.NET streams use ArgumentOutOfRangeException/IOException there), and the test `Invalid_origin_and_overflow_do_not_move_the_stream` pins it as the expected type — an expectation the report does not ask for. No new public API, no changed defaults, no perf cost; only Position's setter routes through Seek internally and it always passes non-negative Begin offsets.
reporterNeed: Reporter (Wwwing301, LiteDB dev @f906a5f8, net8 Linux) found AesStream.Seek unconditionally added PAGE_SIZE to the offset for every SeekOrigin, so Seek(0, Current) advanced the stream by a page instead of being a no-op, Seek(0, End) overshot the logical end, and the return value was the physical (header-inclusive) position rather than the logical one. They wanted logical-coordinate seek semantics for all three origins, with the returned value matching Position.
suggestedAction: Nothing required. Optionally, when replying on the issue, note that the exact reproducer now prints their expected block; if you want to be strict about the Stream contract, swap the `checked` OverflowException for ArgumentOutOfRangeException (and relax that one test assertion), since OverflowException is not a documented Stream.Seek exception.
whatChanged: Seek now resolves the target in logical coordinates first (Begin = offset, Current = this.Position + offset, End = this.Length + offset), rejects negative results, then issues a single absolute `_stream.Seek(position + PAGE_SIZE, Begin)` and subtracts PAGE_SIZE from the result. Tracing the reporter's exact console program against this: start=0, current_return=0, after_current=0, logical_length=8192, end_return=8192, after_end=8192 — byte-for-byte the "Expected behavior" block in the report. This is essentially the reporter's own suggested direction, generalised (they proposed keeping Current/End relative on the backing stream, which would still have returned a physical value for Current/End; the commit converts to absolute, which is strictly more correct).

issueTitle: Query enumerated or disposed on another thread leaks the transaction read lock (SynchronizationLockException, LockRecursionException, checkpoint timeout)
overshoot: Real but mostly the price of the fix, not extra scope. No public API, no changed defaults, no new exception on a path that previously worked. Costs others pay: (a) every transaction enter/exit, plus `IsInTransaction` and `TransactionsCount`, now goes through one global `Monitor` + `Dictionary<int,int>` (TransactionGate.cs) instead of ReaderWriterLockSlim, serializing transaction admission for read-heavy concurrent workloads; (b) dropping the `alreadyLock` skip means nested same-thread transactions each take a lease, inflating `CurrentReadCount`, which `TryEnterExclusive` (LockService.cs:116) uses to decline auto-checkpoints — slightly more skipped checkpoints under nesting; (c) leases are keyed by `Environment.CurrentManagedThreadId`, which the runtime recycles, so a stale lease from a dead thread can make an unrelated thread look "in a transaction" — spurious `AlreadyExistsTransaction` on DropCollection/RenameCollection/SetPragma, or `LockRecursionException` on Checkpoint (RWLS cleaned up dead-thread ownership itself); (d) a thread blocked in the gate when the engine is disposed underneath it now gets `ObjectDisposedException` rather than the old swallowed SynchronizationLockException.
reporterNeed: The issue is a maintainer-written consolidation of six real user reports (#1637, #1712, #1721, #1993, #2017, #2197) with no comments of its own. Those users enumerate a LiteDB query across a thread boundary — `await` inside `foreach (col.FindAll())` in ASP.NET, `Parallel.ForEach` over a lazy `FindAll().Select(...)` calling `FindOne`/`Update` in the body, a Xamarin UI thread plus a timer thread — and get `SynchronizationLockException` (≤5.0.16) or a silently leaked read lock (≥5.0.17) that turns into `LockRecursionException` on the next operation and a `Checkpoint()` timeout, leaving the `-log` file unmerged. They want those ordinary patterns to work instead of having to `ToList()` everything.
suggestedAction: On merge, comment on #2790 and on the closed duplicates (#1637, #1712, #1721, #2017) naming the version that carries the fix and saying plainly whether 5.0.x will get it — every one of those reporters is on 5.0.x, and proposal 4 is still open. Separately, file a follow-up for the abandoned-cursor lease (never-disposed enumerator): either a monitor-side reclaim or an explicit documented contract that a query enumerator must be disposed, because that case now hangs silently instead of throwing.
whatChanged: Replaces the thread-affine `ReaderWriterLockSlim` transaction gate with `TransactionGate`, which counts read leases per owning thread id under a monitor. `ExitTransaction` now takes the owner id and releases `transaction.ThreadID`'s lease rather than the disposing thread's, and only when `TransactionRegistry.Remove` actually removed the transaction (so double-dispose is a no-op and a foreign disposal cannot release someone else's lease). `GetTransaction` no longer skips taking a lease when `FindForThread` says the thread is "already locked", and `ReleaseTransaction` no longer infers ownership from `FindForThread`; nesting on one thread is now a counted re-entry. The `catch {}` that silently swallowed the mis-release since 5.0.17 is gone. Concretely: start-on-A/dispose-on-B now decrements A's lease, so A's next `FindById`/`Insert` succeeds and `Checkpoint()` gets the exclusive lock. Tests cover the #2017 shape (500 docs, `Parallel.ForEach` over lazy `FindAll().Select`, `FindById`+`Update`, then `Checkpoint`), `await` inside `foreach (FindAll())` then `Checkpoint`, and the issue's repro 1 (cursor opened on one thread, disposed on another, owner then reads and inserts, then `Checkpoint`) — the reporters' own scenarios, not adjacent ones.

gap: Item 2 of the issue's own proposed fix is not implemented: `ENSURE(page type must be collection page)` still throws `LiteException.InvalidDatafileState`, which `EngineState.Handle` turns into engine shutdown + datafile marked for auto-rebuild. So if any *other* path still hands a read snapshot an invisible/zero page (e.g. the `DropCollection` race in #2545, or a concurrency path not covered by the publication lock), the blast radius is unchanged: whole engine dies, later calls throw `ObjectDisposedException` / "Maximum number of transactions reached". Nothing in this commit softens that. The reporter's own pattern no longer reaches it, so this is residual hardening, not a live block.
issueTitle: "ENSURE: page type must be collection page" / "Invalid Collection on 0 ... Full zero: True" when a collection is read while another transaction is creating it
overshoot:
One extra behaviour change rides along, beyond what 2792 needs. Moving `GetCollectionPageID` / `GetCollections` / `GetAvailableCollectionSpace` off the `lock(this)` header monitor onto the new `PublicationLock` means snapshot creation no longer serializes behind *any* commit — previously every commit (holding `lock(_header)` across log write + fsync) blocked all new snapshots. Now only commits with header callbacks (collection add/drop/rename) do. That is the #2818 reader-stall improvement, it gets its own new test (`Issue2818ReaderStall_Tests`) in this same commit, and it changes concurrency semantics for every user, not just the reporter's case. It looks sound (all `_collections` mutations and the map read are both under `PublicationLock`; lock order is consistently `_header` → `PublicationLock` → wal `_indexLock`, so no inversion), but it is a second, wider change bundled into a fix for 2792.

Smaller: `Issue2792SnapshotPublication_Tests` pins "a reader must block until publication completes", i.e. it hard-codes design option (a) from the issue and would fail option (b) (treat a not-yet-visible collection as non-existent). It asserts the block by polling `Thread.ThreadState & WaitSleepJoin`, which is a fragile thing to pin in CI. No public API change (`HeaderPage` is `internal`; `CollectionService.Get` signature change is internal).
reporterNeed: Several threads call `db.GetCollection("TableName").FindById("QueryHash")` on a collection that does not exist yet, while one thread creates it with `BeginTrans(); Upsert(); Commit()` (LiteDB used as a per-process query cache, single shared `LiteDatabase`, direct file mode; #2002, plus #1653/#2340 variants). The readers get `LiteDB ENSURE: page type must be collection page` (or "Invalid Collection on 0. Full zero: True" on 5.0.7-5.0.9), and on dev the engine then closes and marks the file for auto-rebuild. They want reads that race collection creation to return null (or the committed doc) instead of throwing, without wrapping every call in an application-level `ReaderWriterLockSlim`.
suggestedAction: When the PR lands, reply on #2792 (and the duplicates #2002/#1653/#2340) that the reader now either sees the collection as not-yet-existing (`FindById` returns null) or sees it fully committed, so the application-level `ReaderWriterLockSlim` workaround can be dropped. Note explicitly that proposed-fix item 2 (a not-yet-visible page must not close the engine / flag the datafile for rebuild) was NOT done here, and either keep 2792 open for it or split it into its own issue so #2545-style zero-page reads stop taking the whole engine down.
whatChanged: Adds `HeaderPage.PublicationLock` and makes collection-map identity and WAL visibility a single atomic pair. `Snapshot`'s constructor now samples `_readVersion = _walIndex.CurrentReadVersion` and `_header.GetCollectionPageID(name)` together inside that lock (previously the read version was sampled outside the header lock and the page ID inside it — exactly the window the issue describes), and passes the resolved pageID into `CollectionService.Get` instead of letting it re-read the live header. On the writer side, `TransactionService.Commit` holds `PublicationLock` across `PersistAndConfirm()` when the transaction has header callbacks (collection add via `CollectionService.Add`, drop via `Snapshot`, rename via `LiteEngine.RenameCollection`), so `OnCommit`'s `InsertCollection` and `_walIndex.ConfirmTransaction` become indivisible to readers. Running the reporter's code: a racing `FindById` now either takes the lock before publication and sees pageID `uint.MaxValue` → `collectionPage == null` → returns null (their `if (data != null)` fall-through works), or takes it after and gets a read version that already includes the confirm → the page resolves from the WAL. The zero-page read, and therefore the engine shutdown, cannot occur on this path. `Issue2792_Tests` is the reporter's own scenario, made deterministic: it gates the header write to the log with `SimulateDiskWriteFail`, runs `FindById("QueryHash")` on a collection being created by `BeginTrans/Upsert/Commit`, asserts neither side throws, tolerates null-or-"published", and re-opens the file afterwards. Pre-fix that reader samples the old read version, blocks on the old `lock(this)` in `GetCollectionPageID`, then resolves the new pageID at the old version — i.e. it reproduces the reported failure.

issueTitle: FileStorage re-upload fails with "LiteDB ENSURE" and downloads are silently truncated after an interrupted (non-atomic) upload
reporterNeed: Users of FileStorage (consolidating #2326/#1268/#2325/#2370/#2518) hit a permanent split between `_files` and `_chunks` after an upload was interrupted (crash, kill, undisposed OpenWrite, source stream throwing mid-copy). From then on re-uploading the same id throws `LiteDB ENSURE` / LiteException 999, and `Download` silently returns fewer bytes than `length` claims — so their file is both unreadable and unrepairable without the undocumented `Delete(id)`-first workaround. They need: re-upload to heal the file, truncated downloads to fail loudly, and an upload that does not destroy the old content when it fails halfway.
whatChanged: All three asked-for items are implemented. (1) `LiteFileStream` write-mode ctor drops `ENSURE(count == _file.Chunks)` and now deletes the id's chunk range unconditionally (previously only when `_file.Length > 0`), so re-upload heals both the "metadata says chunks, none exist" and the "orphan chunks, no `_files` row" states — the duplicate-key error from #2370/#2518 goes away too. (2) `LiteStorage.Upload` wraps OpenWrite+CopyTo+Dispose in `_db.BeginTrans()`/`Commit()`, and on exception calls a new `LiteFileStream.Abort()` (suppresses the flush that used to commit the truncated length) plus `Rollback()`. (3) Read side: the ctor rejects `length`/`chunks` metadata that disagree about emptiness, and `GetChunkData` throws `LiteException.INVALID_FORMAT` ("missing or empty chunk at index n" / "ended before its declared length") instead of treating a missing chunk as EOF. `SharedEngine`/`SharedDataReader` are reworked so the new nested `BeginTrans` does not leak a mutex recursion or dispose an engine it borrowed.
gap: Only `Upload` is atomic. `OpenWrite` — the exact API the reporter used to produce the corruption — still deletes the old chunks in its own auto-commit before a single new byte is written, and still leaves `_files`/`_chunks` disagreeing if the stream is never disposed. The issue's own proposal ("consider the same for OpenWrite streams") is unimplemented, and nothing in the commit tells a user that incremental writers must be wrapped in their own `BeginTrans`/`Commit`. Also, existing damaged databases can no longer be partially salvaged: `Download` throws instead of returning the readable prefix, and the message ("File 'x' has a missing or empty chunk at index 0") does not say that re-uploading the id repairs it.
overshoot: Three things go past the report. (a) A failed `Upload` now rolls back a transaction the caller owns, discarding the caller's unrelated pending writes, and swallows any rollback error (`try { _db.Rollback(); } catch { }`). `StorageAtomicity_Tests.Failed_upload_restores_metadata_and_releases_its_transaction` pins exactly that ("a failed upload rolls back even a caller-owned transaction", caller collection count 0). The report only asked for `BeginTrans` when the thread has none; silently destroying a caller's transaction is a new, undocumented contract for everyone who uses explicit transactions. (b) The read path switched from data-driven to metadata-driven: `GetChunkData` short-circuits on `index >= _file.Chunks` instead of probing `_chunks`. The very `ENSURE` being removed proves that stored chunk counters drift in the wild; a database whose `_files.chunks` is understated but whose chunk data is intact used to download completely and now throws "ended before its declared length". (c) `SharedEngine.BeginTrans`/`CloseDatabase`/`Query` and `SharedDataReader.Dispose` are restructured (nested-transaction mutex recursion, borrowed-engine ownership) — collateral needed by (a) but a change to shared-mode concurrency semantics that every shared-mode user pays for. Minor: every upload of a brand-new file now issues a `DeleteMany` range delete that used to be skipped, and a whole upload is now one transaction rather than per-chunk commits (log growth for very large files; safepointing keeps it from failing outright).
suggestedAction: Keep the fix; narrow (a): roll back only the transaction `Upload` itself started, and let the exception propagate so a caller inside their own transaction decides — or, if the unconditional rollback is intentional, say so in the `Upload` XML doc and release notes instead of only in a test message, and stop swallowing the rollback exception. Consider falling back to probing `_chunks` when `index >= _file.Chunks` so an understated counter is not a new read failure. Then comment on #2806 and the duplicates (#2326, #1268, #2325, #2370, #2518): re-upload of the same id now repairs both missing-chunk and orphan-chunk states, `Download` of a damaged file now throws INVALID_FORMAT instead of returning short data, and `Upload` is atomic — but `OpenWrite` streams are still not, so wrap them in `BeginTrans`/`Commit` yourself and always dispose them.

The issue asked for a message of the shape "add a setter (private is fine) or assign the id yourself"; the F# reporter (#1541), whose actual fix is `[<CLIMutable>]`, gets nothing pointing there, and no docs change accompanies the commit (the issue explicitly asked the object-mapping page to state that an auto-id member needs a setter). Landing 3cc84705f3 without aed800c9a leaves the reporter with an NRE (now rolled back, but still a NullReferenceException from `_id.Setter(entity, ...)` inside the generator), i.e. #2811's headline symptom survives.
issueTitle: Insert with auto-id throws NullReferenceException after writing the document when the Id member has no setter (get-only property, F# record)
overshoot: Contained, but three real behaviour changes beyond the literal report. (1) The id write-back now executes inside the engine's write transaction (`GetBsonDocs` yields, the engine resumes enumeration before commit), so a user property setter with side effects now runs while the collection write lock is held — reentrant LiteDB calls from a setter change semantics. (2) A bulk insert whose write-back fails on document N now rolls back all N-1 earlier documents instead of keeping them; that is the atomicity the issue asked for, but it is a semantic change for callers who tolerated partial bulk inserts. (3) Anyone who was catching the old NRE and relying on the document having been written now gets nothing written. The new `DataTypeNotAssignable` guard (autoId=ObjectId + default setter + member type not assignable from ObjectId, e.g. `string Id` left null) is not overshoot: that path previously threw InvalidCastException from the compiled setter *after* the write, so no working path is lost — it only moves the failure earlier with a better message. Same for the added `IsNull` cases: the engine previously threw `InvalidDataType("_id", Null)`. No new public API (`MemberMapper.DefaultSetter` is internal), no changed defaults, no per-operation perf cost.
reporterNeed: Insert an entity whose Id member has no setter — a get-only `public ObjectId Id { get; }` (#612) or an immutable F# record with `Id = 0` (#1541) — and either have it work or be told clearly why it cannot. Instead LiteDB wrote the document and then threw a bare NullReferenceException from `LiteCollection<T>.Insert` while copying the generated id back, leaving a committed row plus an unexplained crash.
suggestedAction: Two things before closing #2811. (a) Do not land 3cc84705f3 without aed800c9a — the read-only LiteException comes from that commit, and alone this one only makes the NRE atomic. (b) Extend the message in Insert.cs:102-103 to carry the remedy the issue drafted, e.g. "... add a setter (a private one is enough), mark F# records [<CLIMutable>], or assign the id before inserting", and add the docs note the issue asked for. Then reply on #612/#1541 that a read-only auto-id member is not supported by design, that the insert now fails cleanly with nothing written, and name the three workarounds.
whatChanged: Running the issue's exact repro on this tree: `Girl { public ObjectId Id { get; } }` maps as the id member with `Setter == null` (get-only properties are still mapped; only `CanRead` filters `GetTypeMembers`), so `RemoveDocId` throws `LiteException(PROPERTY_READ_WRITE, "Cannot generate an auto ID for read-only member 'Id': it has no setter.")` on the first MoveNext of the lazily-enumerated doc sequence, i.e. before `InsertDocument` runs — `col.Count()` stays 0, exactly the proposal in the issue. The F# `{ Id: int; ... }` record behaves identically (record fields are CanWrite=false). 3cc84705f3's own contribution is the atomicity half: both `Insert(T)` and the bulk/upsert paths now route through `GetBsonDocs(entity, doc)`, which yields the document and performs `_id.Setter(...)` only after the engine resumes enumeration, so any write-back failure aborts the transaction instead of leaving a committed row; plus `IsNull` now counts as an empty id for Int32/Int64/Guid auto-ids, and a pre-write `DataTypeNotAssignable` check when the generated ObjectId cannot be assigned to the id member's type.

gap: No hard cap: any transaction that stays open longer than the 10 ms admission wait (explicit BeginTrans held open, a lazily-enumerated Find cursor consumed slowly, a long write transaction) still starves auto-checkpoint completely, and the log still grows without bound — the commit's own evidence file says so ("explicit/writing/retained transactions may time out and later commits retry. No hard WAL cap") and Issue2814Lifecycle_Tests/Issue2814Backoff_Tests pin that the log stays non-zero while a reader is held. The 10 ms wait is also not escalated as the log grows, so a workload of continuous medium-length queries (each >10 ms) keeps failing admission; attempts are then rationed to once per 50 ms..1 s. Nothing warns or logs when this happens, so an always-on user like #2261 still has to work out on their own that they need periodic db.Checkpoint(). The issue's own second ask — document checkpoint behaviour on the pragma docs page — was explicitly excluded (only LiteDB.ReproRunner/README.md was touched).
issueTitle: Log file (-log.db) grows without bound when other transactions are always open, because auto-checkpoint is skipped instead of retried
overshoot: Modest and bounded, no new public API, no new exceptions, no changed defaults. (1) Read latency cost everyone with concurrent readers now pays: while the committing thread waits up to 10 ms for exclusive admission, TransactionGate blocks all new reader leases (_waitingWriters != 0), so read-heavy callers can see up to 10 ms stalls where previously the checkpoint attempt aborted instantly with zero reader impact; CheckpointBackoff rations this to one waiting attempt per 50 ms..1 s only after a failure, and resets on every success. (2) The non-rationed TryCheckpoint() on the Dispose path (LiteEngine.cs:199) now also waits for readers instead of skipping — benign, arguably desirable. (3) Issue2814_Tests asserts a peak log size <= 8 x soft limit under 4 live reader threads; that is a timing-dependent bound that may flake on slow or loaded CI (this repo already has known ARM64 flakes). (4) TransactionMonitor.GetTransaction reordering (lease before ID reservation) is a real correctness companion to the change, not scope creep.
reporterNeed: Users running a shared LiteDatabase with a steady writer plus continuous concurrent readers (#2125: bulk InsertBulk with 50 FindById tasks; #1764: 6 GB log in hours; #2261: always-on service) saw the -log.db grow until the disk filled, because auto-checkpoint was skipped on every commit whenever any other transaction was open. They wanted the log to be checkpointed back into the data file on its own, without having to call db.Checkpoint() manually or restart the process.
suggestedAction: Comment on #2814 stating the scope honestly: auto-checkpoint is now admitted between short concurrent readers, so the #2125-style writer+FindById workload keeps a bounded log; but a transaction held open longer than the ~10 ms admission wait (explicit BeginTrans, a slowly consumed Find cursor, a long write transaction) still starves the checkpoint and the log still grows unbounded, with periodic db.Checkpoint() remaining the workaround. Then close the issue's two remaining items separately: the pragma documentation update, and a decision on whether a hard WAL limit / pragma (the issue's original proposal) is wanted for the long-transaction case.
whatChanged: LockService.TryEnterExclusive gained waitForReaders/milliseconds, so a checkpoint can queue behind existing readers instead of bailing out the instant CurrentReadCount > 0; because TransactionGate blocks new reader leases while a writer waits, a 10 ms wait drains short in-flight readers and the checkpoint gets in. The commit path calls the new TryAutoCheckpoint, rationed by CheckpointBackoff (50 ms doubling to 1 s, reset on success) so a long-lived reader does not make every commit stall 10 ms; commits inside the back-off window still checkpoint when no transaction is open. TransactionMonitor.GetTransaction now takes the read lease before constructing the transaction so a concurrently admitted checkpoint cannot reset the WAL ID sequence under a transaction that already reserved an ID.

gap: Two of the issue's own proposal items are not in this commit: (3) no fallback to Flush(false) / no connection-string opt-out where durable flush is rejected, and (4) the documentation durability statement (the thing #1251 asked about) is still uncorrected, so a reader still has no written answer about when LiteDB fsyncs. Users on UNC/network shares (#2242) get no knob at all.
issueTitle: Committed transactions are lost on power loss or OS crash: commits never fsync the log file, and encrypted databases never fsync at all
overshoot: Failure semantics go well past the report. Any exception from the new per-commit flush — including non-IO ones such as the `UnauthorizedAccessException` that `FileStream.Flush(true)` throws on UNC shares (#2242, real stack trace in that issue) — is wrapped into `IOException` and fed to `_state.Handle`, which permanently stops the engine (rollback and every later write then throw; user must dispose and reopen). Previously commit only did `Flush(false)`, so a network-share database failed at most at checkpoint/dispose; now it dies on the first insert, with no fallback, although the issue explicitly proposed "fall back to Flush(false) where Flush(true) is rejected". `LiteDB.Tests/Internals/WalDurability_Tests.cs` pins that escalation (InvalidOperationException must surface as IOException, rollback and next write must throw) — an expectation the report does not justify. Secondary: an fsync on every confirmed commit with no opt-out is a throughput cost every user pays (the issue listed `Flush=false` as an optional escape); safepoint-only batches and empty commits are correctly exempted, which limits it.
reporterNeed: Data that LiteDB reported as committed (auto-commit insert or explicit Commit) disappears after a blue screen or power cut, because v5 never fsyncs the log on commit — and for encrypted databases (`Password=`) nothing is ever forced to disk. v4 had a `Flush=true` connection-string option; v5 removed it, leaving users of client PCs with encrypted files (#2155, #2156) losing their latest committed writes with no setting to prevent it.
suggestedAction: Before merge, add the fallback the issue's own proposal item 3 asks for: if `Flush(true)` is rejected by the stream (UNC/network share, `UnauthorizedAccessException`), degrade to `Flush(false)` (or expose a connection-string opt-out) instead of wrapping into IOException and stopping the engine — otherwise #2242's users regress from "throws at dispose" to "engine dead on first insert". Then land the documentation correction and post it as the honest answer on #1251/#2155/#2156.
whatChanged: In `DiskService.WriteLogDisk`, the batch now tracks whether any written page has `P_IS_CONFIRMED`; if so the log stream gets `FlushToDisk()` (a real `FileStream.Flush(true)`, routed through `AesStream`/`ConcurrentStream` wrappers by the pre-existing helper) before the lock is released, so `Commit()` returns only after the WAL is on stable storage — for plaintext and encrypted files alike. Batches without a confirmation (safepoints, empty commits) keep the cheap `Flush()`. A flush failure is turned into an `IOException` and handed to `_state.Handle`, which stops the engine.

issueTitle: Opening a file that is not a v5 LiteDB database modifies it: files under 8 KB are overwritten with an empty database, larger ones are truncated
reporterNeed: #2820 consolidates three real reports: #2277 (an app probes files with `new LiteDatabase(path)` and falls back to an old serializer on exception — LiteDB rewrote the old files), #2434 (a v4.1.4 db opened on 5.0.18 without `Upgrade=true` throws and is left truncated, afterwards unopenable by v4 or v5 even with Upgrade), #2501 (a 16-byte text file is opened and written to; a ~16 KB one throws after truncation). All three want the same thing: a failed open must throw and leave the file byte-identical, and a v4 file must still be upgradeable afterwards.
whatChanged: Adds `DiskService.ValidateExistingData()`, called in the DiskService ctor for any non-new data file: it rents a read-only stream, reads page 0, throws INVALID_PASSWORD if byte 0 is 1, and constructs `HeaderPage` to validate identity/version — all before `_dataPool.Writer.Value` is ever materialised, so no writable handle is opened for a foreign file. `TrimTrailingPages` moves to its own partial file (unchanged logic; still called from LiteEngine.Open after the header parses, and skipped when ReadOnly). Both engine stream factories now build `new AesStream(password, stream, allowRecovery: false)`, and AesStream gains two new throws under that flag: a non-empty stream shorter than PAGE_SIZE, and the "check bytes 32..64 are all zero" branch. Note the bulk of what the reporters needed (side-effect-free `FileStreamFactory.GetLength`, the `dataLength < PAGE_SIZE` throw, trim-after-validation, and the `InvalidFile_Tests` + encrypted-v4 fixture tests) already landed in the ancestor commit d744bec52 "Reject invalid database inputs without modification"; this commit's distinctive delta is the AesStream lockdown plus the earlier header check.
gap: #2434's reporter still gets the generic "File is not a valid LiteDB database format or contains a invalid password" for a v4 file. The issue's own item 4 (detect a v4 header and say "v4 data file, open with Upgrade=true") is not implemented, so a user holding a v4 file still has to find `Upgrade=true` themselves — the file is no longer harmed, but the message does not point at the remedy.
overshoot: `allowRecovery: false` is passed from every engine path (FileStreamFactory and StreamFactory, data file, log file and temp/sort file), which silently reverts closed issue #2343. #2343's corrupted file is exactly 8192 bytes with byte 0 = 1, salt at 1..16 and zeros from 17 on; AesStream recovered it via `isNew = checkBuffer.All(x => x == 0)` at offset 32..64. That branch is now `if (isNew && !allowRecovery) throw LiteException.InvalidDatabase()`, so such a file is permanently unopenable instead of self-healing. Because `CreateLogFactory` uses the same password and factory, an interrupted `.log` creation now hard-blocks opening a database whose `.db` holds real user data. Second guard: `!allowRecovery && Length > 0 && Length < PAGE_SIZE` throws for a partially written encrypted preamble (e.g. 17 bytes) — the very case #2820 item 3 says to keep re-initialising ("This keeps the existing recovery case from #2343"), and it makes `FileStreamFactory.GetLength`'s partial-preamble branch (returning 0 when the first byte is 1 and length < PAGE_SIZE) unreachable as a recovery path. No test in the commit shows a legitimate interrupted-creation file still recovering; instead `OpenValidation_Tests` InlineData(16384, "secret", …) pins the opposite by building the zeroed-32..64 shape and asserting INVALID_DATABASE. Minor extra cost: every open of an existing database now reads and parses page 0 twice (DiskService then LiteEngine).
suggestedAction: Narrow the AesStream change rather than revert it: keep recovery allowed for the writable stream that DiskService opens when it has already decided the file is new/partial-preamble (or pass the decision down explicitly), and keep `allowRecovery: false` only for the validation/read path used to reject foreign files. Add a regression test for the #2343 shape (8192-byte encrypted file with 32..64 zeroed, created by LiteDB) still opening, and either honour or delete the now-dead partial-preamble branch in `FileStreamFactory.GetLength`. Separately, implement issue item 4 (v4 header detection with "open with Upgrade=true") or post that sentence as a comment on #2434 so its reporter knows the remedy.

issueTitle: Explicit transactions are bound to the OS thread, so BeginTrans/Commit/Rollback across await act on the wrong transaction
reporterNeed: 2822 is a maintainer-written consolidation of real user reports (#1771: `Commit()` returns false after an `await` and the writes are silently lost; #2373: ASP.NET Core/gRPC needs more than one transaction per thread; #2363: ThreadLocal tracking breaks async). Users want an explicit transaction that survives a continuation hopping threads — or, failing that, to not lose data silently and to be told what to do instead.
whatChanged: Implements exactly the issue's own "short term" list, and only that. (1) `LiteEngine.Commit()` now routes through `GetTransactionForCompletion`: when the calling thread has no transaction but some other thread has an active `ExplicitTransaction`, it throws a `LiteException` naming the rule ("BeginTrans, writes, Commit and Rollback must run synchronously on the same thread; do not await inside the transaction") instead of returning false. (2) `Rollback()` deliberately still returns false in that situation, so it does not replace the exception a catch/finally block is handling. (3) A `ThreadLocal<bool>` abort mark (`MarkExplicitAbort`/`ConsumeExplicitAbort`) suppresses the throw when the engine itself already rolled this thread's transaction back after a failed operation. (4) `ExplicitTransaction` is now set only on a genuinely new transaction (`if (isNew)`), previously unconditional but dead state. (5) SharedEngine: `Commit`/`Rollback` unified behind `CompleteTransaction`, holding an extra mutex recursion; foreign `Commit` throws, foreign `Rollback` returns false; nested `BeginTrans` no longer leaves `_transactionRunning` stuck true; new `RejectAbandonedTransaction` disposes the orphan engine and throws "owner thread exited" when the transaction's owner thread died. (6) `docs/explicit-transactions.md` plus XML-doc updates on `ILiteDatabase`/`LiteDatabase` documenting same-thread ownership and nested-join semantics.

issueTitle: Rebuild() on an encrypted database: parameterless call leaves a plaintext file ("File is not encrypted"), password change throws "Invalid password"

Before this commit that same call also ended with a plaintext file, but it threw `LiteException: File is not encrypted` — the data-at-rest outcome is unchanged, the loud signal is gone. The same applies to SQL `REBUILD {"collation":"..."}` (LiteDB/Client/SqlParser/Commands/Rebuild.cs builds a fresh `RebuildOptions` and only sets Password when the JSON has one). gap: The report's explicit-transaction acceptance criterion — "the next write from another thread must succeed" — is deliberately not met: after a failed Rollback()/Commit() the whole engine is stopped, so every thread and collection fails until the LiteDatabase is disposed and reopened. The previously working recovery ("Calling Rollback() again recovers") is gone. No test covers a second thread that is blocked on the collection lock at the moment Close() disposes _locker/_monitor, so what that thread sees (clean IOException vs ObjectDisposedException/SemaphoreFullException vs hang) is still unverified. For non-IOException completion failures Stop() stores the raw exception, so a later unrelated Insert rethrows e.g. "InvalidOperationException: completion failed" with no "engine closed, dispose and reopen" wording — the user gets no hint the engine is dead (TransactionCompletion_Tests pins exactly that: BeSameAs(injected)).
issueTitle: When Rollback() or Commit() throws, the transaction is never released: locks stay held and later auto-transaction writes are silently lost
overshoot: Stop() is now triggered by ANY exception escaping transaction.Commit()/Rollback()/ReleaseTransaction, not just IOException/INVALID_DATAFILE_STATE as before. A non-IO failure (ENSURE/LiteException, ObjectDisposedException, a throw from snapshot.Dispose, or a throw from ReleaseTransaction after a commit that already durably succeeded) now takes the entire engine offline for all threads, where previously it left the engine usable. That is a wider blast radius than the report needs — the report's harm was one leaked/dead transaction — though the reporter himself offered "mark the engine invalid" as an option. Also note the report's first proposed remedy (ReleaseTransaction in a finally) was not implemented; cleanup now depends entirely on Close() disposing the monitor, so if Close() short-circuits (state already Disposed, or origin != _state) the transaction stays registered. Minor: an unused `SimulateDataWriteFail` field was added to EngineState.
reporterNeed: When Rollback() or Commit() itself throws, LiteDB skipped _monitor.ReleaseTransaction, so the transaction stayed registered and locked. For an explicit transaction other threads timed out on the collection lock; for an automatic transaction (bulk insert hitting a duplicate key, whose auto-rollback then fails) later Insert calls on that thread returned success but ran inside the dead transaction and were silently lost after reopen. The reporter wanted the transaction released and later writes to either commit or fail loudly — never to silently vanish.
suggestedAction: Before merging PR #2918, wrap non-IOException causes in Stop() with the same "Engine closed after ... Dispose and reopen the database before retrying" context (keeping the original as InnerException) so a later operation's exception explains itself, and relax the TransactionCompletion_Tests BeSameAs assertion accordingly. Then reply on the issue stating explicitly that the explicit-transaction path was resolved by killing the engine rather than by releasing the transaction and letting other threads continue, so "Rollback() again recovers" is intentionally no longer supported. Optionally add a two-thread regression test for a writer blocked on the collection lock when the engine is stopped.
whatChanged: Commit()/Rollback()/AutoTransaction now route completion through CommitAndReleaseTransaction/RollbackAndReleaseTransaction, which catch any exception and call the new EngineState.Stop(ex) before rethrowing. Stop() CAS-installs the first failure (wrapping IOException with "Engine closed after an I/O failure. Dispose and reopen...") and calls LiteEngine.Close(ex, origin), which disposes the monitor (releasing every transaction and its locks) and the disks; Validate() then throws that stored failure for all later operations. The AutoTransaction catch also gained a `transaction.State == Active` guard so a half-committed transaction is not rolled back again. Net effect for the reporter: the silent-loss window is closed — the post-failure Insert now throws instead of returning success and disappearing — and the leaked locks are released by the engine shutdown.

issueTitle: Large single-transaction inserts and deletes are 3-4x slower since the 1,000-page default (safepoint cost)
overshoot: Small and mostly contained. `TakeIdleWritableLocked` (LiteDB/Engine/Disk/MemoryCache.Writable.cs:80-97) mirrors what `EvictLocked`/`TransitionToFreeLocked` (MemoryCache.cs:261-309) already did — `_index.Remove`, `_sharedReads.Forget`, `Generation++` — so stale `BufferSlice`s throwing after the transfer is pre-existing eviction semantics, not a new failure mode. No public API, no changed default, no new validation, no new exception on a path that used to work. The one cost others pay: a write to a page that is momentarily idle in the read cache now removes that cache entry, so the next reader of that position takes a disk read where it previously got a cache hit (the old code kept the readable copy and memcpy'd). For read-while-write workloads on hot pages that is a real, unmeasured trade-off; the PR measures read throughput and working set (79 -> 76 MB) but not this specific effect. Test churn in `Cache_Tests`/`FrameFailure_Tests` (moving `source.Release()`, `PinnedPages` 0 -> 1) is a consequence of the new hit path, not an unjustified expectation.
reporterNeed: The reporter (the maintainer, self-filed) measured that after #2772 lowered the per-transaction page limit to 1,000, one large insert went from 2.8s to 8.6-12.9s and a large delete from 1.8s to 7.1-8.0s at default settings, while `transaction pages=100000` restored 3.4s/2.2s. They did not want the default raised back; they wanted the safepoint itself made cheaper (profile it, avoid re-writing unchanged pages, avoid a flush per safepoint, consider scaling the limit with the cache budget) plus a benchmark to track it.
suggestedAction: Before merging, drop "Closes #2849" from PR #2918 and leave the issue open (or close it and immediately file the follow-up), because the commit recovers roughly half the regression. Post on #2849 the same-harness before/after numbers for this commit alone — the evidence file only has post-change default vs large-budget — and state plainly that the default remains ~1.65-1.83x the large-budget setting, that `transaction pages=100000` is still the escape hatch, and that the unchanged-page-skip, per-safepoint flush and cache-budget-scaled limit ideas plus the requested insert/DeleteMany benchmark are still open.
whatChanged: `MemoryCache.GetWritablePage` moves to a new partial file and gains an idle-hit fast path: when the cached readable frame for the position has `ShareCounter == 0`, ownership of that frame is transferred to the writer under `_sync` (removed from `_index`, forgotten by `_sharedReads`, generation bumped, state -> Writable) instead of acquiring a second frame and `Buffer.BlockCopy`-ing 8KB into it. Pinned (in-use) frames still take the old copy path. This cuts one frame allocation plus one page copy per re-dirtied page, which halves cache pressure in the safepoint loop the report blames. The single caller is `DiskReader.ReadPage(writable: true)`. Tests added: three `MemoryCacheWritableOwnership_Tests` for the transfer/copy/race semantics, and `Issue2849CacheWrite_Tests` which checks commit/rollback/recovery correctness under `TransactionPageLimit=16` for plain and encrypted engines.
